title: Testing the Politicians
next_title: How Many Things I Do Not Need
lesson: Confidence is not the same as knowledge.
lines: Socrates' first target: a famous politician. Everyone in Athens said he was brilliant.
Excuse me, said Socrates. What is justice? Easy, said the politician. Justice is... whatever I say it is.
And what makes you right? Because I'm important. And what makes you important? Because I'm right!
Round and round they went, in circles, like a dog chasing its own tail.
The crowd began to laugh. The politician turned red with anger. Socrates had just made an enemy.
Socrates walked away, thinking: He doesn't know, but he thinks he knows. I don't know, and I know I don't know.
The loudest voice in the room isn't always the wisest. Confidence is not the same as knowledge.
Next time: Socrates goes shopping, and buys nothing. Follow so you don't miss it!
